sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 3767 of 2023

Petitioner :- Gaurav Kumar Singh
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Deptt. Of Home Lko. And Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Sampurna Nand Shukla,Pankaj Shukla

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sangeeta Chandra,J.
Hon'ble Narendra Kumar Johari,J.
(1) Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.G.A. who appears on behalf of the State Respondents.

(2) This petition has been filed with the following main prayers:-
"ii) Issue a writ order of direction in the nature of certiorari thereby quashing the impugned F.I.R. dated 26.4.2023 on Crime No-0238/2023 Under Sections- 493,
498A I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition-Act, 3(2)(5) SCST Act, Police station- Kotwali Nagar, District- Raibareli,, as contained in Annexure No-1 to the petition, in the interest of justice.

Gaurav Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11563138/
1 iii) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the respondents/opposite parties not to arrest the Petitioners or to use any coercive methods, during pendency of the writ petition, or during investigation proceedings in the interest of justice."
(3) It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the opposite party no. 4 only to force the petitioner to marry her has lodged the impugned F.I.R. and falsely implicating him under Sections 493, 498-A of the I.P.C. alongwith Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and Section 3(2) (5) of the S.C./S.T. Act.

entities.text: Gaurav Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He says that none of the ingredients of Section 493 are made out.

(4) This Court has gone through the definition of offence as mentioned under Section 493 of the I.P.C., it is quoted here in below:-
"493. Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of

lawful marriage.-Every man who by deceit causes any woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine."
(5) This Court has also perused the F.I.R. and finds that a cognizable offence is made out.
(6) The present writ petition stands dismissed.
